hook.text: A phone call drops when you enter an elevator. The signal didn't disappear—it faded as reflections canceled each other.

buildup.text: Fading occurs when multiple copies of a signal arrive via different paths and interfere destructively.

discovery.text: Rayleigh fading models this: signal strength fluctuates wildly as you move even a small distance.

twist.text: MIMO antennas exploit multipath: they turn fading from an enemy into extra data paths for higher throughput.

climax.text: 5G uses massive MIMO—dozens of antennas working together to combat fading and boost capacity.

punchline.text: Reflections fight you. Smart antennas fight back.

quiz.question: What causes multipath fading?
options: Signal copies arriving via different paths and interfering
Too many users on the network
